clue.text: Mislaid files found above the stage

definitions.note: a location phrase standing for the noun: the space above a stage

indicators.note: things mislaid are put in the wrong place, so these letters end up out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Lost paperwork turns up in the theatre rigging above the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Above the stage' reads as part of the story about the files, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In a theatre, the flies are the space high over the stage where scenery is hung.

clue.text: Bogus saving rationale

blocks.note: bogus means not genuine
economy is the principle of saving money or resources

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a cost-cutting argument as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the two parts of the phrase are simply defined in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A false economy is a supposed saving that ends up costing more in the long run.

clue.text: Necessity delivers a novel idea

blocks.note: surface reading: need produces something
setter's reading: the proverb says necessity is the mother of the thing in the answer, so she gives birth to it
a new idea or device that nobody had before

explanation.surface: Being in need produces something new.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'Necessity is the mother of invention' turns 'delivers' into giving birth.
explanation.definitionFit: An invention is something newly devised, a fresh idea or contrivance.

clue.text: Clever sting!

blocks.note: first meaning: quick-witted or intelligent
second meaning: to feel a sharp burning pain

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation suggests admiring a clever con trick (a sting), but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for intelligence and a verb for a sharp stinging pain.

clue.text: Ill-treated lag's first uneasy, deep sleep leads to impaired vision

indicators.note: something ill-treated is knocked about, so the letters are knocked out of order
the first of the following word means only its opening letter is kept

blocks.note: lag is a convict, taken as written for rearranging
the opening letter of uneasy
a coma is a state of deep unconsciousness

explanation.surface: A mistreated prisoner sleeps badly and ends up with damaged eyesight.
explanation.walkthrough: A lag is British slang for a convict.
explanation.definitionFit: Glaucoma is an eye disease in which raised pressure damages the optic nerve and harms sight.

clue.text: Godless seen to go round in an odour of sanctity

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An atheist makes the rounds with an air of holiness.
explanation.walkthrough: IN goes between the fourth and fifth letters of Godless; nothing is shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: The odour of sanctity is an air of saintliness, so it stands for piety or holiness.

clue.text: New man receives a point for the last word

indicators.note: a new version of a word has its letters made over in another order
receiving something means taking it inside

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
E is east, a compass point

explanation.surface: A newcomer is given a point and gets the final say.
explanation.definitionFit: Amen is said at the very end of a prayer, so it is literally the closing word.

clue.text: Figure to solve a mathematical problem

blocks.note: first meaning: to work out or reckon
second meaning: to work out an answer with numbers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' looks like a noun, a number, but it is a verb meaning to reckon.
explanation.definitionFit: To calculate is to reckon or work out by arithmetic, which covers both phrases.

clue.text: New motive to take time out to see film

indicators.note: to take something away, with the 'out' that follows, is to remove it from the word
with 'take', out means removing that thing from the word
a new version of a word has its letters made over in another order

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone with a fresh reason takes a break to catch a film.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove T from motive and rearrange the five letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: A movie is the American term for a cinema film.

clue.text: Active at the beginning and end of dental treatment, having a tolerant attitude

indicators.note: placing a word at both the start and the finish means it is written twice, framing the rest
treatment works material over, so the letters are reworked into a new order

blocks.note: a live wire or volcano is active; placed at the beginning
taken as written, to be rearranged
the same word again, placed at the end

explanation.surface: A patient who stays lively through dental work is admirably easy-going.
explanation.walkthrough: LIVE is written at both ends with the rearranged dental in between; the definition is a phrase, so the phrasal answer reads as an attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Live and let live is the motto of tolerance: put up with how others choose to behave.

clue.text: Grumpy when gum cured, treated exclusively

indicators.note: something treated is processed and altered, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
exclusively means solely

explanation.surface: A dental patient is still bad-tempered after the gum disease is fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Curmudgeonly describes a bad-tempered, cantankerous person, a close synonym of irritable.

clue.text: Nineties' reform explained by theoretical physicist

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters are reshaped into another order

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A political shake-up of the 1990s is accounted for by a scientist's theory.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein, author of relativity, is the most famous example of a theoretical physicist.

clue.text: Office in old town in beautiful French surroundings

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it
surroundings enclose whatever is in them

blocks.note: beau is French for beautiful
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city

explanation.surface: An office set in a pretty old French town.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur, the ancient city in Iraq, is a crossword favourite for 'old town'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bureau is an office or agency, as in a travel bureau or the Federal Bureau of Investigation.

clue.text: Yearn somehow to follow fashionable deception

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters come in some other order
following means coming after, so this part goes second

blocks.note: chic means stylish
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Longing to keep up with fashion leads to trickery.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicanery is trickery or underhand dealing used to gain an advantage.

clue.text: CIA angels in disguise giving relief from pain

indicators.note: a disguise changes the appearance, so the letters are rearranged to look different

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Undercover American agents bring comfort to the suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, analgesic means relieving pain, the property of a painkiller.

clue.text: A Beatles hit not very long ago

blocks.note: first meaning: the 1965 Paul McCartney song
second meaning: the day before today

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the song is fairly recent, a joke since the hit is from the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a famous Beatles ballad and the day just past, a recent time.

clue.text: Discrimination is infiltrating the annual general meeting

indicators.note: something infiltrating gets inside an organisation, so it goes within the other part

blocks.note: the usual abbreviation
taken as written

explanation.surface: Prejudice has crept into a company's yearly shareholder meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Agism (also ageism) is prejudice against people because of their age.

clue.text: Concentrated on the kind of treatment an ICU could provide

definitions.text: the kind of treatment an ICU could provide

blocks.note: first meaning: thorough and focused

blocks.clueFragment: the kind of treatment an ICU could provide
blocks.note: second meaning: the care given in a hospital unit whose initials begin with I

explanation.walkthrough: ICU stands for intensive care unit, so the answer is the I of those initials.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means concentrated and focused, and also names the highest level of hospital care.

clue.text: Fourteenth-century warrior's origins not in National Jordanian Archives

indicators.note: the origins of words are where they start, so only their opening letters are kept

blocks.note: the opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: The roots of a medieval fighter cannot be traced in Jordan's records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not in' looks like an instruction to exclude something, but those two words supply letters too; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninjas were covert Japanese fighters, said to date from feudal times in the 1300s.

clue.text: Had doubts about an unreliable journalist

blocks.note: suspect means not to be trusted
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: Someone distrusted a reporter who could not be relied on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unreliable' looks like an anagram signal, but it supplies a word of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: To have suspected something is to have mistrusted it or felt doubtful of it.

clue.text: Slander Frenchman put in place

blocks.note: M is short for monsieur
to align is to set in position

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is defamed and put firmly in his place.
explanation.definitionFit: To malign someone is to speak ill of them falsely, the same as slandering.

clue.text: Animal for student priest

blocks.note: L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates
a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk or priest

explanation.surface: A trainee clergyman is assigned a pet.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain an L plate marks a learner driver, hence L for student.
explanation.definitionFit: A llama is a South American animal of the camel family, kept for wool and as a pack beast.

clue.text: Judgement given in words that make sense

blocks.note: first meaning: the punishment a court decides
second meaning: a grammatically complete group of words

explanation.walkthrough: 'Given in' seems to say how the verdict was delivered but is only the join.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a court's punishment on a convicted person and a complete grammatical unit of language.

clue.text: Unspoken diplomacy one accepted

indicators.note: something accepted is taken in, so the other part holds it

blocks.note: tact is diplomatic sensitivity
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An unspoken diplomatic understanding was agreed on.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means understood or implied without being said aloud in words.

clue.text: Tie with some untanned rawhide

indicators.note: some of a phrase means only a part of it, lying within the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the join between the two words

explanation.surface: Fastening something with a strip of raw leather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tie' suggests binding with the rawhide, but it means a level result in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A draw is a match ending level, with neither side winning: a tie.

clue.text: Industrialisation of output service first

indicators.note: first means this part comes at the front, ahead of the word before it

blocks.note: Mass is a church service
production is what is produced

explanation.surface: Factory output is put first as a nation industrialises.
explanation.walkthrough: The parts are read in reverse of the clue's order because 'first' moves the service to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Mass production, making goods in great quantity by machine, is the hallmark of industrial economies.

clue.text: Watch hay being strewn at entrance

indicators.note: strewn things are scattered about, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Look out for straw scattered at a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatchway is an opening in a deck or floor that gives access, a kind of doorway.

clue.text: New York's after Peg Little

indicators.note: after means coming behind, so this part goes second

blocks.note: a tee is the peg a golf ball sits on
NY is the abbreviation; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A small woman named Peg is chased by New York.
explanation.walkthrough: Peg looks like a woman's name, but it is the golf peg.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeny is a childlike word for very small, a variant of tiny.
